SEO and GEO are not the same game, and treating them like they are is costing you visibility.

SEO gets you ranked in a list of ten blue links. Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) gets you cited by name inside a single AI-generated answer, whether or not anyone ever clicks through to your site.

Strong SEO still helps here. Research shows solid Google rankings correlate with more AI mentions. But it's just an input now.
If your content plan is still 100% built around ranking, you're optimizing for half the buyer journey.

repost.content:
Over the last few years with the rise of AI, I've watched something erode across B2B organizations: the muscle of critical thinking, the willingness to sit with a hard problem long enough to actually understand it, the curiosity that makes someone ask why a strategy isn't working instead of just firing your marketing leader, the taste that tells you when something is genuinely differentiated, the empathy required to understand what a buyer actually needs

This happens because the pressure is real. Leaders have to fly the plane while rebuilding it through a thunder storm. Since 2022, building and running a B2B company has gotten harder. The world is telling these companies to adapt, to automate, to accelerate. And in that noise, something important gets lost. The things that actually drive long-term business success: sharp positioning born from genuine market insight, messaging that earns trust because it reflects real buyer understanding, creative that works because someone cares enough to make it good. These are not things a model generates. They are things people build, learn, discern and create. 

AI is great. I use it. We use it at Refine Labs. There are a lot of great use cases for this techology. But it’s far too easy to outsource everything to a machine. And because humans will often take the path of least resistance, that's exactly what most people are doing.

The things that truly matter in marketing, and in business, can't be outsourced to a machine. Not because the machine isn't capable of providing an answer, but because the act of doing them is how you find the right answer. The judgment you develop by working through a hard strategic problem. The taste you build by caring about quality over time. The empathy you earn by actually listening to your customers. These aren't inputs to a process. They are the process.

The Refine Labs Marketing Maturity Model is not something we built by feeding data into a system and extracting a framework. It was built by working closely with over 300 B2B marketing organizations, asking hard questions, observing patterns that only become visible when you're paying close attention, and making judgment calls about what actually matters. The insights in it are the product of curiosity and critical thinking applied over 7 years.

Most B2B marketing organizations are not underperforming because they lack resources or effort. They're underperforming because they're executing the right tactics in the wrong order, at the wrong stage of organizational maturity, without the foundational work that makes those tactics compound. They're running hard without a map. And, in a world that is changing fast and in a role carrying immense pressure to perform - the map is how we can navigate the turbulence to find success. This model we have codified is the map.

Check out the free version of the assessment we built here: https://lnkd.in/gx77HgHK

Most B2B marketers today own exactly one of the 4Ps: Promotion.

And even with that, they're losing to AI-scaled outbound and FUD-driven performance ads.

Product strategy? Founders and engineering. 
Price? Finance or whatever the competitor charges. 
Place? A LinkedIn feed and maybe a Gartner listing if you're lucky.

This is what the 4P handoff looks like in practice, and it's happened so quickly that most marketing teams don't realize how much ground they've already given up and how much of a losing position they are working from before they even step into a new role.

Tomorrow Liam Moroney and I are going live to talk about how to start taking back more of the 4Ps of marketing even if you can't own them outright, including:

Why synthetic research is a cop-out that won't save you
How you can get more influence over Price by doing what others won't
What to do about "place" when your product doesn't exist in a store
Why your promotion strategy is one offer design exercise away from working

Marketers have to stop being the most replaceable person in the room. Being proficient in AI will help. Being more of an authority for the company outside Promotion is how you make yourself irreplaceable.

Wednesday, May 20th at 11am ET: https://lnkd.in/eigGtvhm

This is for B2B marketers tired of being handed a demand gen budget and told to perform. Who know the only way Promotion works is by having the other 3 Ps work harder for them and need to find ways to take some of it back under their purview.

posts.content:
More companies are replacing buyer research with AI-generated insights.
Copying their competitors pricing instead of testing their own.
Basing their channel choices on what everyone else is doing.
Promoting where the ROI appears in a quarter or it’s a failure.

And all of this is making the marketing profession more and more irrelevant and outsourceable to AI.

It's faster. It's cheaper. And it's often misleading or even outright wrong.

AI doesn’t have personal goals. 
It doesn't have subjective emotions. 
It doesn’t have memory in any meaningful sense. 
It doesn't behave like real buyers.

What you miss when you stop talking to your market: the real reason people don't buy your product is almost never about features. It's migration complexity. Reporting breaking. Team adoption friction. Things AI will never surface because it requires doing the unglamorous work of getting to know your market really well.

We know there are hundreds of live events, webinars, and LinkedIn Lives on all the Promotion hacks out there to squeeze a few more sales leads in a month to get you to your MQL goal.

But too few want to talk about how to take some control back into the other parts of the marketing profession that make that Promotion work sustainably in Brand, Demand, and Expand motions.

So I asked the busiest guy on the Live Event circuit recently Liam Moroney to join me, put an actionable agenda up, and discuss ways marketers can start to own more than just Promotion in small ways en route to owning more the 4Ps going forward.

We’re not going to magically take it back all at once. But there are real ways and ample evidence for why and how you can start to claw back some of the Product, Place, and Price responsibilities back under your purview to help drive the business forward to greater heights.

most companies aren't using AI wrong because they picked the wrong tool...they're using it wrong because they skipped the thinking part.

We're seeing it everywhere right now - teams cranking out more content than ever, reaching fewer people than ever. Faster output, weaker signal.

AI is genuinely useful. We use it. But the teams getting real lift from it are using it to think better, not to think less. They're stress-testing ideas, moving through options faster, freeing up space for actual strategy.

The moment you hand judgment over to the tool is the moment you lose your own voice, your own perspective, your own personality.

The answer to better marketing is still people who know how to make meaning out of information - AI just helps them do it faster.

Non-ICP customers close slower, close at lower rates, churn more, and eat up resources that should be going somewhere else.

A real ICP isn't a brainstorm exercise or a slide in a deck. It's a data-informed definition built from actual customer signals and validated against pipeline and revenue outcomes.

When sales, marketing, and product align on that picture, everything downstream gets sharper. Targeting, messaging, roadmap, retention.

ICP clarity is one of the fastest growth levers most teams aren't pulling.
